neet_phy_u10_t10_1.working: For a string fixed at both ends, f1 = v/2L = 200/(2×0.5) = 200 Hz.

neet_phy_u10_t10_2.working: Closed pipe: f1 = v/4L = 340/3.4 = 100 Hz. Only odd harmonics occur, so the second overtone is the 5th harmonic = 500 Hz.

neet_phy_u10_t10_3.working: 4 antinodes means 4 loops, so L = 2λ and λ = 0.6 m. Then v = fλ = 250×0.6 = 150 m/s.

neet_phy_u10_t10_4.working: A is true: closed pipe f = v/4L, open pipe f = v/2L. R is also true as a general fact. However, A follows from the end boundary conditions (displacement node at the closed end, antinode at the open end), not directly from R. So R does not explain A.

neet_phy_u10_t10_5.working: 7th harmonic: L = 7λ/4. Displacement nodes lie at 0, λ/2, λ and 3λ/2 from the closed end, giving 4 nodes, so I is correct. A standing wave has no net energy transport, so II is incorrect.
